chapter: Chapter 1. The Building Blocks of Risk Management
stem: A junior analyst at a bank is asked to provide suggestions on potential metrics the bank can use in its capital management program. The analyst prepares a presentation discussing the advantages and disadvantages of the RAROC metric. Which of the following statements is most appropriate for the analyst to include in the presentation?
stem_short: Which statement about RAROC belongs in the presentation?

options.A: RAROC will make it easier to compare the profitability of business divisions that require different levels of capital.
options.B: RAROC allows the firm to benchmark its performance against operating targets set by industry peers.
options.C: RAROC is an effective forward-looking tool to model potential extreme losses during stress scenarios.
options.D: An activity is adding value to the bank’s shareholders if its cost of equity capital is higher than its RAROC.

answer_points.title: RAROC puts every business line on the same scale

B.reason: Not a peer benchmark — it tests units against your own cost of equity.

C.reason: Built on expected returns — stress losses need scenario analysis.

D.reason: Backwards — value is added when RAROC beats the cost of equity.

takeaway.text: Adds value only if RAROC > cost of equity
Not a peer benchmark or stress test

sections.text: [warmly] Hey, welcome back to Risk Hub! FRM Part 1, Book 1, Foundations of Risk Management. Chapter 1, The Building Blocks of Risk Management. Let's do another practice question.

So, a junior analyst at a bank is asked to suggest metrics for the bank's capital management program. The analyst puts together a presentation on the pros and cons of RAROC... that's risk-adjusted return on capital. Which statement belongs in that presentation?

Option A. RAROC will make it easier to compare the profitability of business divisions that require different levels of capital. Option B. RAROC allows the firm to benchmark its performance against operating targets set by industry peers. Option C. RAROC is an effective forward-looking tool to model potential extreme losses during stress scenarios. And option D. An activity is adding value to the bank's shareholders if its cost of equity capital is higher than its RAROC.
Okay, pause the video and lock in your answer. [long pause]

[excited] And the answer is... A! [warmly] Here's why. Different business lines need very different amounts of economic capital, and RAROC puts them all on the same footing. You take the risk-adjusted return and divide it by the economic capital it uses. So a small desk and a big lending unit can finally be compared apples to apples.

Now, why not the others? B is wrong. RAROC isn't a peer benchmark. It tells you whether your own business units earn more than your cost of equity capital. C is wrong too. RAROC is built on expected returns. It doesn't model extreme losses in a stress scenario... for that, you'd use tools like scenario analysis. And D has it backwards. An activity adds value when its RAROC is higher than the cost of equity capital, not lower.

[warmly] So, the key takeaway. RAROC compares business lines that use different amounts of capital. A business adds value only when its RAROC beats its cost of equity. And it's not a peer benchmark or a stress test. If this helped, follow Risk Hub for more FRM practice. See you in the next one!
